title: H2 – Sustainable HRM
source: Zusammenfassung von Session 1, Teil „Sustainable HRM“ (Folien 19–26, Festing; Stahl et al., 2020)

blocks.text: Sustainable HRM (Ehnert et al., 2016) adopts HR strategies and practices that achieve financial, social and ecological goals, inside and outside the organisation, over the long term, while controlling for unintended side effects.
The triple bottom line (Elkington, 1997) – social, ecological, financial – is the lens: sustainable HRM is about managing trade-offs between the three.

Compared with strategic HRM, the sustainable philosophy looks beyond the firm's boundaries, is longer-term, combines top-down and bottom-up control, is integrated with operations, proactive and activist, and treats the three performances as equally important.
Firms adopt sustainable HRM for compliance, instrumental/strategic or mission-led reasons (Stahl et al., 2020); only the last two go beyond the law.
HR can harm by commission (actively contributing to a problem) and by omission (failing to prevent one) (Brewster & Brookes, 2024).

children: Triple goals · inside & outside · long term · control of side effects
Instrumental: fit strategy, attract talent, impress investors
Mission-led: do the right thing, consistency with values
Financial: ESOPs, long-term leadership development, retention, TBL incentives for managers
Ecological: hire for sustainability values, link green behaviour to promotion, eco-education
Social: volunteering, healthy work environment, health investments, no child/forced labour in the supply chain, decent pay

blocks.text: Sins of commission and omission (Brewster & Brookes, 2024)
children: Commission: excessive pressure, biased algorithms, precarious contracts, extreme pay gaps, layoffs for short-term profit
Omission: ignoring harassment, pay inequality, unsafe conditions, discrimination in promotion, not reskilling workers threatened by AI

blocks.text: Score each HR option on the three TBL dimensions and name the trade-off explicitly.
Check the four elements of the definition: is the effect long-term, does it reach outside the firm, is there an unintended side effect?
Identify the firm's motive (compliance, instrumental, mission) – it tells you how far the firm will go and how to sell your recommendation.
Look for sins of omission – what HR tolerates is easy to miss in a case text.

HRM strategies and practices that enable financial, social and ecological goals, inside and outside the organisation, over a long-term horizon, while controlling for unintended side effects and negative feedback (Ehnert et al., 2016).
Corporate performance measured on social (people), ecological (planet) and financial (profit) dimensions (Elkington, 1997).
HR contributes actively to a harmful outcome / HR fails to prevent a harmful outcome (Brewster & Brookes, 2024).
Brainstorm: name three HR practices that create a sustainability trade-off (e.g. AI-based recruitment: financial + but social − through bias; remote work: ecological + but social ±).
